issues.legal_issue: An ejectment application under the statutory procedure for land of public utility is available only when the land has the specified customary pasture status.
material_facts: An application was made to eject the tenant on the ground that the land was customary common pasture land.
The revenue records described the land as parti, including parti fit for cultivation, and did not record it as customary pasture land.
The evidence did not show that the land had been used as customary common pasture land or as pasture land.
issues.conclusion: The land did not fall within the description required for an ejectment application under the statutory procedure. The officer acted without jurisdiction, and the ejectment order was illegal, null and void, and not binding on the tenant.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 212-A(1) and 212 of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, an application for ejectment under section 212-A could be made only if the land was recorded as customary pasture land or was customary common pasture land. Because neither condition was established, the officer lacked jurisdiction to order ejectment.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_ejectment_order and not land_recorded_as_customary_pasture and not land_was_customary_common_pasture

predicates.appeal_challenges_ejectment_order: A party appealed against an order ejecting a person from land under a special procedure for land of public utility.
predicates.land_recorded_as_customary_pasture: The land was recorded in the relevant records as customary pasture land.
predicates.land_was_customary_common_pasture: The land was in fact customary common pasture land.
predicates.ejectment_order_is_invalid: The ejectment order is invalid and does not bind the person ordered to be ejected.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an ejectment order and the land was neither recorded as customary pasture land nor shown to be customary common pasture land, the rule treats the order as invalid.

issues.legal_issue: An ejectment order under the statutory procedure is not final against an affected person who brings a suit to establish the claimed right.
material_facts: An ejectment order was made against the tenant under the statutory procedure.
The tenant brought a suit under the provision allowing a party against whom such an order was made to establish the right claimed.
The suit sought a declaration that the order was not binding and that the tenant held rights in the land.
issues.conclusion: The ejectment order was not final, and the suit to establish the claimed right was maintainable. The order becomes conclusive only if the suit brought by the person sought to be ejected fails.
issues.legal_principle: Section 212-A(7) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act permits a party against whom an ejectment order has been made to institute a suit to establish the claimed right; the order becomes conclusive subject to the result of that suit and is conclusive only if the suit fails.

predicates.ejectment_order_under_special_procedure: An order was made to eject a person under a special statutory procedure.
predicates.affected_person_brings_rights_suit: The person against whom the order was made brought a suit to establish the claimed right.
predicates.rights_suit_is_maintainable: The suit to establish the claimed right is maintainable.

issues.definition: If a person subject to an ejectment order under a special procedure brings a suit to establish a claimed right, the suit is maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: Land may be held for purposes connected with agriculture without being wholly under cultivation, and a hereditary tenant who holds land for those purposes on the date immediately preceding vesting qualifies for sirdar status.
material_facts: The land was let to the tenant for growing crops, and she brought a substantial portion under cultivation.
She paid rent to the intermediaries and regularly paid revenue to the State.
The courts below found that she lawfully continued to hold the land for purposes connected with agriculture.
The revenue records showed that she held the land as a hereditary tenant on the date immediately preceding vesting.
issues.conclusion: The tenant satisfied the requirements for sirdar status and became a sirdar of the land on the date of vesting.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3(14) and 19 of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act apply where land is held or occupied for purposes connected with agriculture and is held by a person in the specified hereditary-tenancy category immediately before vesting. Actual cultivation is not essential if the land is held for an agricultural purpose. The word “held” is broad and includes possession by legal title, as interpreted in Budhan Singh v. Nabi Bux; the distinction between holding and occupation was also supported by R. v. Ditcheat.

rule.if: tenancy_status_determined_at_vesting and land_held_for_agricultural_purpose and holding_based_on_legal_title and person_was_hereditary_tenant_before_vesting

predicates.tenancy_status_determined_at_vesting: A proceeding determines whether a person acquired the statutory status attached to land at vesting.
predicates.land_held_for_agricultural_purpose: The land was held for a purpose connected with agriculture, whether or not all of it was actually cultivated.
predicates.holding_based_on_legal_title: The person held the land under a legal title, such as a tenancy granted by the person entitled to let it.
predicates.person_was_hereditary_tenant_before_vest: The person held the land as a hereditary tenant on the date immediately preceding vesting.
predicates.person_acquires_sirdar_status: The person acquires sirdar status in the land on vesting.

issues.definition: When a proceeding determines status at vesting, and a person held land under legal title for an agricultural purpose as a hereditary tenant immediately before vesting, the rule gives that person sirdar status.
